results.explanation: The fixed source establishes an application capability but not the actual deployment result. (1) The visible gates are POST /signin, ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH being true, a configured trusted-email-header name selecting this branch, presence of that named header, and authenticate_user_by_email yielding a user. (2) When the branch is selected, the request value under the configured header name is lowercased into email and passed to authenticate_user_by_email; no additional client-credential check is shown between those steps in this crop. (3) If authentication returns a user, that returned user object is passed to create_session_response with set_cookie=True, binding the selected email lookup result to the authenticated session resource. (4) The strongest visible application controls are the password-auth entry gate, configuration and presence of the named header, and the requirement that email authentication produce a user. The accepted policy adds a deployment control not implemented or evidenced by these sources: a trusted reverse proxy must be the sole reachable ingress, remove client-supplied identity headers, and inject the authenticated identity itself. (5) The protected effect is reachable on the source-visible branch where password auth is enabled, the trusted-email-header setting is truthy, the named header is present, and email authentication returns a user. (6) The effective ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH value, configured trusted-email-header name, externally reachable ingress set, proxy stripping/replacement behavior, proxy authentication outcome, and selected-email authentication result can change the deployment answer; none is supplied as an actual deployment observation. (7) The optional provisioning branch checks whether the email already exists and, if absent, invokes signup_handler with that same request-derived email before authenticating by email. Thus it can create the identity that is subsequently looked up, but it does not itself create the session; for an already existing selected user, the visible condition skips provisioning. At most six relevant branch summaries are: password auth disabled blocks with 403; password auth enabled but no trusted-header configuration does not select this shown path; configured branch with the named header absent blocks with 400; header present but authentication producing no user cannot reach the shown session effect; authentication producing a user with policy-compliant ingress prevents an external client from choosing the injected identity under the accepted policy; authentication producing a user with a reachable ingress that preserves a client-supplied identity header would allow that value to select the session identity and would fail the deny expectation. Which deployment branch applies is unknown. Other sign-in modes are expressly omitted and unexamined, as are signup_handler internals, authenticate_user_by_email internals, session-response internals, middleware, proxy configuration, and network topology; the fixed crop is not evidence of repository-wide or all-entry completeness.

facts.statement: The supplied entry is POST /signin, and it checks ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH before reaching the trusted-email branch, returning 403 when that gate is false.
The trusted-email branch is selected only when WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER is truthy; within that branch, absence of the configured header name causes a 400 response.
The trusted email, name, groups, and role header names are environment-controlled values; the trusted email header defaults to None when not configured.
The value of the configured trusted-email request header is lowercased and assigned as the email identity used by the branch.
The display name defaults to the request-derived email and may instead come from the optionally configured trusted-name header after URL decoding.
If no user exists for the request-derived email, the branch invokes signup_handler with that same email and generated credentials before attempting email authentication.
The request-derived email is passed to authenticate_user_by_email, and subsequent trusted-header processing is conditioned on that call yielding a user.
The user object produced by email authentication is the user object passed into create_session_response.
When user is truthy, the shown code returns a session response and requests cookie setting; otherwise it returns invalid credentials.
Within the shown trusted-email path, reaching the session effect requires traversal of the password-auth gate, trusted-header branch and header-presence check, followed by a truthy user result.
The supplied source explicitly omits handling for other sign-in modes, so those paths are unexamined in this assessment.

decisiveMissingFacts: The actual runtime value of ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH.
The actual runtime value of WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER, including the exact selected header name.
Which ingress paths an unauthenticated external client can actually reach, including whether the application is directly reachable around a proxy.
Whether every reachable ingress removes any client-supplied configured identity header and replaces it only after authenticating the upstream principal.
Whether the ingress authentication outcome constrains the injected email to the authenticated external principal rather than accepting an arbitrary client choice.
Whether authenticate_user_by_email yields the selected existing user for the request-derived email in the actual deployment.
suggestedObservations: Read the effective runtime values of ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH and WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER from the deployed process or its resolved configuration.

Enumerate externally reachable ingress paths and verify whether any path reaches the application without the trusted proxy; this must include direct service, alternate load balancer, and port exposure checks appropriate to the deployment.

At each reachable ingress, use a controlled test identity to trace a client-supplied configured email header and observe the header delivered upstream, confirming removal and authenticated replacement rather than preservation.
Verify the proxy's effective authentication and header-injection configuration and correlate an authenticated test principal with the exact email value delivered to the application.

Using a controlled existing test user, observe whether the trusted-email request reaches authenticate_user_by_email and whether a session cookie/response is created; test both an attempted arbitrary client header and the proxy-authenticated identity.
